strings.intro: Drag each card onto the line where you think it belongs, or tap a card and then tap the line. There is no right answer key. The point is where you put it, and why.
strings.armed: Now tap the line where this belongs, or pick one:
strings.placedAll: All fifteen placed. Tap any card to see what makes it arguable, or drag it again.
strings.compareSoon: Coming once a class has run it. For now, run it with yours in teacher mode.
strings.hands: Hands up. Tap a column for each hand.

cards.text: Asked an AI to explain a concept from class, then wrote the essay alone.
cards.consider: How is this different from asking a tutor or a friend? And what if the explanation was wrong?

cards.text: Asked for an essay outline, then wrote the essay from it.
cards.consider: The words are yours. The structure isn't. Would you say so anywhere in the essay?

cards.text: Pasted a finished essay in and asked it to fix the grammar.
cards.consider: Where does fixing grammar end and rewriting begin? What if it changed one word and the meaning with it?

cards.text: Asked it to rewrite a paragraph "to sound better".
cards.consider: The ideas are yours and the sentences are not. Does this assignment grade the sentences?

cards.text: Had it write the essay, then rewrote every sentence in your own words.
cards.consider: Paraphrasing someone else's essay is still their essay. Does it matter that the someone is a machine?

cards.text: Used it to translate a source written in another language.
cards.consider: Translation tools have been allowed for years, with limits. Does the school's rule on translation cover this?

cards.text: Made flashcards from your class notes with it, then studied them.
cards.consider: Nothing was handed in. Is there any question here at all?

cards.text: Asked it to solve one maths problem, then solved five similar ones alone.
cards.consider: A worked example is what a textbook gives you. What if it solved the first one wrong?

cards.text: Asked it to solve the whole problem set and copied the working.
cards.consider: Is there any reading of this that isn't copying?

cards.text: Generated the images for a poster and didn't say so.
cards.consider: Nobody is grading the poster. Does credit only matter when there is a mark?

cards.text: Had it summarise a 40 page reading instead of reading it.
cards.consider: You now know what the summary says. Do you know what the reading says?

cards.text: Checked your essay against the rubric with it before handing it in.
cards.consider: A teacher could do this too. Is it different when the checker also suggests the fixes?

cards.text: A teacher made the worksheet with AI and didn't tell the class.
cards.consider: Students must disclose even a whiff of AI in brainstorming. What is the rule for the person who sets the rule?

cards.text: A teacher used AI to give feedback on every student's draft.
cards.consider: Where did the drafts go? Did the students know? Did the teacher read what it said before they did?

cards.text: A teacher put an AI-generated poster up in the corridor with nothing saying so.
cards.consider: Students say they can tell, and that they hate it. Who is the poster for?
